author: val
body: This chapter did not compile on its own until 2026-07-28. It calls text-drop and text-take from Foreword chapter StringUtils at seven sites and did not cite it, so it resolved only when something else in the compilation unit happened to cite StringUtils. A foreword chapter contributes its names only when cited, which is the rule DevelopersRulebook records, and this was the failure it predicts. Now cites StringUtils, CCE and Parse explicitly.

author: val
body: Digits are tested with CCE's is-digit, never against a literal band. This function compared char-code-at against 51 and 61 until 2026-07-28, and CCE digits are 3 through 12: measured char-code-at "0" 0 = 3 and "9" 0 = 12. The test could therefore never succeed and NO ordered list was ever recognised; every numbered item parsed as a plain paragraph. md-has-dot-space carried the identical band.

author: val
body: The literals 65 and 2 are the CCE code points for '.' and ' ', and both were MEASURED correct on 2026-07-28 while the digit band beside them was wrong. That is why they are still literals: the chapter's author got two of the three constants right, so the error was partial, not a wholesale ASCII assumption. Anyone re-checking should measure rather than assume in either direction.

author: val
body: The item number comes from num-text through text-to-integer. It was hardcoded to 1 until 2026-07-28 while num-text was computed and discarded, so once the recognition defect above was fixed every item would have rendered as '1.'. The two had to land together: fixing recognition alone would have shipped a visibly wrong number. text-to-integer is safe to lean on here because parse-decimal-loop uses CCE's own is-digit and digit-value rather than a band of its own.

author: val
body: Every arm here calls rich-text-to-plain, so ALL styling is discarded at widget conversion. The parse side is correct and was measured so on 2026-07-28: '**bold**' yields a run with ts-bold True, '*ital*' ts-italic True, and '[lbl](url)' ts-underline True with tr-link 'url'. All of it is then thrown away and every block becomes a plain widget-label. This is the same shape as the DetailPane badge colour: computed correctly, discarded at render, and NOT fixable here, because a WidgetNode carries no style and the only per-node channel is the WkCustom tag, which no renderer reads. Recorded rather than fixed; the decision is wider than this chapter.

author: val
body: Duplicates rich-text-plain-text in UI chapter RichText exactly: same loop, same bounds, different name. They agree today. Two definitions of one operation that agree by luck rather than by construction is how the key-tab collision started, so if either changes, change both or delete one.
